messages:
Olivia - CS: FYI — incoming escalated ticket from AcmeRetail: intermittent partial streaming responses after reconnect. customer says sometimes they get a truncated final chunk, other times they see the full output duplicated after reconnect. looks related to token rotation on their client side.
AcmeSupport (customer): Hi, we saw two strange things: 1) stream closed mid-generation, when we reconnected we got the missing tail twice in one session; 2) other times the resumed stream didn't include the last sentence and we had to re-request which created a duplicate generation in our logs. cc @support
Maya - Support Eng: Can you paste the client's reconnect logic? asking because duplicate final output = either server retried the generation or client re-requested without idempotency.
AcmeSupport (customer): Here's a simplified version of our SSE reconnect flow (we rotate auth token every 5m):
```
// pseudo-node sse client
const connect = () => {
  fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } })
    .then(res => {
      res.body.on('data', onChunk)
      res.body.on('end', () => setTimeout(connect, 1000))
    })
}
// tokenRotation updates `token` in-place
```
We also log resume_token returned by your stream but we just re-open and pass the new Authorization header.
Rohan - Eng-ML: Hmm. important detail: if client rotates Authorization and server ties resume_token to the original session principal, server may treat the reconnect as a new client and start a new generation instead of resuming, or accept the resume but spuriously re-send buffered chunks. Do we have runtime logs for their session id / resume_token?
Kai - SRE: RuntimeBot shows two events for session 7f3: `session_resume_attempt resume_token=abc123 by principal=acme-user@t=170` then `generation_start id=gen-712 source=resume? false`. Later `generation_complete id=gen-712 tokens=342` and then `generation_start id=gen-713 source=manual_reconnect` then `generation_complete id=gen-713 tokens=342`. So looks like server both accepted a resume and then also started a new generation — race between resume acceptance and client sending a new create request.
Maya - Support Eng: That matches customer's observed duplicates. They said sometimes they get the tail twice (two completed generations with identical token sequence) and sometimes only partial output (resume accepted but missing last chunk). Likely a race where resume accepted but missing last buffered chunks due to internal flush ordering during token rotation.
Olivia - CS: Customer impact = duplicate billing on some reconnects, truncated outputs on others. They want recommended client changes + an immediate mitigation on our side.
Rohan - Eng-ML: Immediate mitigation: make resume acceptance atomic w.r.t. any in-flight create request for the same session id. If resume_token validated, server should return the last_sent_cursor and pause any new generation creation until either resume completes or a short TTL expires. Also ensure we de-duplicate generation IDs: if a generation with identical seed & cursor completes twice, mark second as duplicate and avoid billing increment.
Kai - SRE: Short-term workaround for customer: 1) include idempotency_key in the initial create (so if client re-requests while reconnecting we dedupe), 2) don't rotate Authorization mid-stream — instead use a refresh token flow where the client fetches a fresh token and re-opens only after stream fully closes or after exchanging a short-lived handoff header.
AcmeSupport (customer): Oof, rotating mid-stream is part of our security posture. Can you recommend exact repro steps so our devs can test with a controlled script?
Maya - Support Eng: Repro script we used: 1) start SSE stream with long generation (simulate by prompt that yields many tokens) 2) after N tokens, rotate token on client and re-open connection passing new Authorization + resume_token header 3) optionally send a fresh create request immediately after reopen to simulate a client that doesn't wait for resume confirmation. I can paste the curl sequence: 
```
# open initial stream (server returns resume_token=abc123)
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer OLD" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?prompt=long > stream.log &
# after 2s, rotate token and re-open
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer NEW" -H "Resume-Token: abc123" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?resume=true > stream2.log &
# immediately trigger a create call that would start a generation if resume not accepted
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer NEW" -d '{"prompt":"same prompt"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Rohan - Eng-ML: Good. I'll reproduce in staging but two product questions: 1) do we expose resume compatibility across principals (if token rotates to equivalent user identity) or require same credential? 2) how do we surface resume acceptance to client? right now client only sees subsequent token chunks; not a single definitive accept/reject event.
Kai - SRE: We currently validate resume_token against session+user fingerprint. If Authorization header principal doesn't match original, we still accept if the refresh flow indicates same underlying identity, but that check is fuzzy and racey. We should tighten: resume_token should carry a short-lived guard sig that is verifiable independent of Authorization header (so token rotation won't break atomic resume). Also add an explicit control-frame event `:resume_ack: status=accepted|rejected last_cursor=...` emitted before any resumed chunks.
Maya - Support Eng: Agreed — adding a resume_ack event will let clients decide whether to de-duplicate or trigger a fallback create. We'll propose: server emits resume_ack then after that either resumes streaming from cursor or returns resume_rejected and client can safely call generate.
RuntimeBot: Noted. Filing runtime ticket RUNTIME-5943 to: implement resume_ack control frame, tie resume acceptance atomic to generation lock, and add duplicate-generation billing dedupe by generation-hash.
Rohan - Eng-ML: For the billing dedupe we'll compute generation-hash = sha256(model+seed+prompt+cursor) and only bill first successful write. We'll need to consider non-deterministic model outputs (sampling) — but for now dedupe identical token sequences or identical hashes when using deterministic sampling.
Olivia - CS: Can we offer AcmeRetail a temporary credit for duplicate billing while this is investigated?
Maya - Support Eng: Yes — recommend 100% credit for duplicate generation IDs observed between timestamps 1917001100-1917001300 and offer to set their account to a non-rotating token for a week while we patch.
AcmeSupport (customer): Appreciate that. We'll try the suggested client change (wait for resume_ack or keep token steady) and run your repro script. Please keep us updated.
Kai - SRE: I'll attach the staging repro results here by EOD. Rohan, assigning you RUNTIME-5943. Maya, I'll send the credits request to billing.
Rohan - Eng-ML: Repro plan: spin up model emulator with intentionally slow flush, run curl sequence, capture stream.log and stream2.log, compare token sequences, verify duplicate gen IDs and race windows. Will also test resume_ack implementation in a feature branch.
Olivia - CS: Thanks team. I'll update the customer thread with the mitigation and the ticket refs. :+1: :eyes:
